items.prompt: Email from "Nusantara Bank": "Dear Customer, your account will be blocked in 1 hour. Verify at this link." Which phishing signs appear?
choices: A generic greeting, time pressure, and a request to verify through a link
None, banks often send emails like this
items.explanation: All three signs appear at once. Official banks don't ask you to verify your account through an email link.

items.prompt: This email is phishing. Tap all the warning signs.

parts.text: Enter your old and new password in this form.

items.explanation: The sender's domain isn't nusadigital.test, there's time pressure, and the email asks for a password. The greeting and closing on their own are harmless.

items.prompt: An email from your coworker's real address asks you to buy vouchers, saying they're in a meeting and you shouldn't call. What's the best move?
choices: Buy them right away, the address is real
Escalate, then confirm with your coworker another way
Just ignore it without telling anyone
items.explanation: Your coworker's account may have been taken over. Escalating lets the security team check the account and protect other people.

items.prompt: An unknown number sends you the file Undangan.apk ("Invitation") through chat. What do you do?
choices: Just open it, it might be an old friend
Don't open it, delete it, and report it if it's on a work device
Forward it to the group so others can check it too
items.explanation: Real invitations are pictures or PDFs, not apps. Forwarding it only spreads the trap to other people.
